title.en: Source, model and runtime provenance panel

summary: Expose what came from a source, what was computed or authored, and what is only a display transform, with stable identifiers that link visible claims to their lineage.
objective: A viewer can tell which dataset/entity, transformation/activity and runtime presentation produced a selected result, including version, units, uncertainty and not-run status where applicable.
applies_when: A scene visualizes supplied data, a numerical model, generated geometry or a scientific claim.
Display transformations could be mistaken for source or simulated values.
intent_signals: show whether this geometry is sourced simulated or illustrative
provenance panel for selected data point
example_prompts: For a forecast playback, show the source dataset, transformation version and current rendered timestep separately.
For an anatomical mesh, distinguish supplied segmentation, authored repair and display exaggeration in the selection panel.
negative_signals: Calling a citation a runtime validation.
Showing a source URL without the model version or transformation that produced the visible value.
not_for: A complete PROV serialization requirement for every artistic scene.
Credentials, private paths or raw research logs.

principles: Organize the panel around the visible result: source entity, transformation/model activity, responsible tool or agent where useful, and the current runtime/display state.
Keep factual provenance separate from artistic rationale. “Sourced,” “computed,” “authored illustration,” “display-transformed” and “not run” answer different questions.
Stable IDs join selection to provenance; labels and URLs alone are insufficient when several versions or transformations share a name.
implementation: In Blender, attach stable public IDs and compact source/model references to named objects or scene data. Export selected custom properties only after sanitization; Blender maps enabled custom properties to glTF extras without defining their namespace.

In Three.js, validate and map extras into an application provenance store. Render a semantic panel outside the canvas with source title/version, transformation/model version, units, uncertainty and runtime check status appropriate to the selected claim.
Keep raw paths, credentials, prompts and private logs outside the asset. If lineage is unavailable, show unknown or unavailable rather than inventing a source.
observable_checks: Selecting two derived objects shows distinct entity IDs and the correct shared or separate activities; changing the display gain does not rewrite source values.
A source link, model version, units and runtime status remain readable after resize and export of the public report; missing fields display explicitly.
Inspect the GLB JSON and public panel: only allowlisted extras appear, and no local path, token, private prompt or raw memo is present.

creative_affordances: Use a compact badge, expandable lineage table or node-link view depending on complexity.
Explain an artistic intervention in plain language next to formal lineage when it affects interpretation.
known_limits: W3C PROV supplies a conceptual vocabulary; this profile does not require or claim a complete conforming PROV document.
glTF extras are application-specific and do not make provenance interoperable without an application contract.
No GLB inspection, source-link test or runtime provenance UI was run.

claims.statement: W3C PROV-DM describes provenance through entities, activities, derivations, agents and responsibility, with extensibility for domain-specific information.
claims.scope: Conceptual organization for a user-facing panel; no full PROV serialization or trust assessment is asserted.

claims.statement: The glTF specification defines extras as application-specific data and recommends a JSON object for portability; Blender 4.5 exports selected custom properties into the corresponding glTF extras without a defined namespace.
claims.scope: Transport mechanism only; sanitization, schema, semantics and UI are application responsibilities.
